subject: Error messages after updating R and rstanarm

messages.author: d684e03f1e47f704
messages.subject: Error messages after updating R and rstanarm
parts:
Hello,


we fitted Bayesian linear mixed models and the script was running fine with a previous R version (3.3.0 on a Mac x86_64-apple-darwin13.4.0; rstanarm 2.9.0-4).

m1 <- stan_lmer(formula =  invRT ~ morphPriming + semPriming + phonPriming + (1 | VP ) + (1 | verb ) + ( 0 + morphPriming | VP) + ( 0 + semPriming | VP)+ ( 0 + phonPriming | VP) ,
                prior_intercept = normal(-1, 1),  
                prior = normal(0, 0.1),
                prior_covariance = decov(regularization = 2),
                data = oneDat,
                chains = 4,
                iter = 2000,
                cores = 4)


After updating the system R and rstanarm (R version 3.3.3; rstanarm version 2.14.1), I get the following error message:


Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) :
  Exception thrown at line -1: []: accessing element out of range. index 4434 out of range; expecting index to be between 1 and 4433; index position = 1v
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done
Fehler in check_stanfit(stanfit) :
  Invalid stanfit object produced please report bug


Does anybody have an idea what could be the issue and how could it be resolved?

Kind regards,

Tina

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Error messages after updating R and rstanarm
parts:
On Tuesday, April 4, 2017 at 12:23:57 PM UTC-4, Mati wrote:
Does anybody have an idea what could be the issue and how could it be resolved?

I would say to try to install rstanarm from GitHub

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstanarm/

to see if it has already been fixed, and if not, file an issue. It probably has to do with the multiple (? | VP) terms not counting up the number of parameters correctly.

Ben

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Error messages after updating R and rstanarm
parts:
Hi Tina, 

I think this is indeed fixed in the development version (and will be in the next release). To install from github in the meantime you can use the devtools package:

devtools::install_github("stan-dev/rstanarm", args = "--preclean", build_vignettes = FALSE)

Let us know if that doesn't work. 

Jonah
